description: Show the SQL a change to the project's tables would run, without running any of it. Posts the change to /api/admin/schema/plan — it changes nothing, writes no files, and works on the managed development database. Read this before proposing a schema change: it names every statement and marks the ones that destroy data.

patches.description: The edits, in order, as the Studio's schema editor sends them. Each names its table by slug and has an `op`: createTable { table: { name, columns, rls, … } }, deleteTable { table }, addColumn / changeColumn { table, key, column, before? }, renameColumn { table, key, to, column }, removeColumn / moveColumn { table, key, before? }, addRelation / changeRelation { table, name, relation: { kind, target, … } }, removeRelation { table, name }, setRls { table, rls }, addRule / replaceRule / removeRule { table, rule?, index? }, setOption { table, option, value }. A column is its definition as data, e.g. { type: { kind: "text" }, notNull: true }.

project.description: The project to act on: a registered project's name (rebase_project_list), or a Rebase Cloud project's slug or id. Optional when the session's directory is linked to the intended project. Refused when it names a different project than the directory's link.

name: rebase_schema_plan
